unknowns.text: A fact that has not been established is unknown, not false. If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the case cannot be approved.

computed.text: Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share.

rules.text: For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. If no control person is identified, request documents.

Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly. Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share. If ownership is not complete, request documents.
Verify the identity of every identified individual. If any is unverified, request documents.
The entity's registry filing must be less than 12 months old. Otherwise request documents.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes. Approve is last in `order`, and a case gets it when no other rule applies. Incomplete is the `unknowns` outcome, from 2.2.
Sets `order`: decline, escalate, request_docs, incomplete, approve.
Sets `unknowns`. A rule that might apply because of an unknown fact leads to incomplete, which is the section 1 outcome for an unestablished required fact.

Handled through the `excluded` fact. The people list's `empty_ok_when` uses it, and so do the excluded conditions in `counts_when`, control-person-missing and ownership-incomplete. Excluded entities need no beneficial owners or control person identified.
This section also defines the control person as an identified individual for non-excluded entities. That is the first branch of the people list's `counts_when`.

Defines the 25%-or-more owners as identified individuals. That is the second branch of `counts_when`. The computed fact open_ownership_pct is unaccounted_pct plus the shares held through excluded entities owning less than 25%. This assumes the pack's unaccounted_pct does not already include shares held through excluded entities, since those are supplied separately in excluded_owners. The SOP does not say whether a named person below 25% could combine their share with unaccounted shares to reach 25%. This translation does not cover that case.
This applies to every entity, including excluded ones, as written.
The SOP does not say whose match counts. This translation uses the same scope as 4.1: the entity and the identified individuals. 'Potential' in the pack means not yet cleared.
The materiality bar is built into the pack's adverse_media facts ('meets the SOP's bar'). The SOP attaches no outcome to its search-recording requirement, so that requirement is listed in `needs`.
The listed industries are mapped to 'prohibited' in maps.industry.
Money services businesses map to 'msb' and virtual currency maps to 'crypto' in maps.industry.

This conflicts with 5.2 as written. Every MSB is escalated by industry-restricted, and escalate outranks approve under 2.1, so this rule can never decide a case. It is left unrepaired for a person to resolve.
A person's location is taken to be their residence.
